subject.title: Feature request: Auto-send intent/acknowledgment text message before agent processing

question: Should OpenClaw solve visible pre-processing acknowledgement text as shared `messages.ackText` config, a non-terminal send-and-continue hook, or only channel-specific placeholder features?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds user-visible config or plugin/channel API and overlaps several channel-specific placeholder proposals, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve shared config
options.body: Add a default-off `messages.ackText` contract with scope and per-channel/account overrides, then align schema, help, docs, tests, and selected channel implementations.

options.title: Approve hook-first API
options.body: Add a documented non-terminal plugin/channel hook for interim sends before model dispatch, leaving channel-specific UX policy to plugins.

options.title: Keep channel-specific only
options.body: Close or narrow this cross-channel issue and let Slack, Telegram, Discord, and Feishu pursue separate placeholder behavior without a shared core contract.

recommendation.title: Approve shared config
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `messages.ackText` contract with scope and per-channel/account overrides, then align schema, help, docs, tests, and selected channel implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is recent dispatch and reply lifecycle work in the central path this feature would touch.
